channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: AI’s ‘Weak-Link Asymmetry’ Gives Hackers a Huge Advantage
item.description: Weighing the likely costs and benefits of artificial intelligence is endlessly complicated, and steering policy with this trade-off in mind could prove impossibly difficult. One issue in particular shows why the problem might be insoluble — and it isn’t yet widely understood.
item.dc:creator: Clive Crook

item.title: Kevin Warsh's Call for a Less Talkative Fed Falls on Deaf Ears
item.description: Upon becoming chair of the Federal Reserve in May, Kevin Warsh pledged to run a tight-lipped central bank, one where decisions about the future path of monetary policy are made amongst policymakers behind closed doors rather than providing so-called forward guidance in public. Six months later, Warsh seems to be having a tough time getting any of his fellow Fed colleagues to go along.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: From Hormuz to Ukraine, and AI to Nuclear Weapons, the World Is Stuck in Limbo
item.description: “We are in the midst of a rupture, not a transition,” according to Mark Carney, the prime minister of Canada. That’s how he, as leader of a “middle power,” sees the world since its formerly benevolent hegemon, America, turned “predatory” under President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth

item.title: Nvidia, AI Stocks: Wall Street Needs to Get Honest on Forecasts
item.description: As global equities tumble into correction territory, Wall Street is searching for catalysts that will bring investors back. Strategists are calling clients to buy the dip, to little avail. Asian governments’ increasingly heavy-handed market stabilization measures haven’t revived animal spirits, either.
item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.title: Trump Makes Anti-Brexit Case Better Than Anyone. The EU Makes the Pro-Brexit One
item.description: No one makes the case for the UK rejoining the European Union more eloquently than Donald Trump, who despises the bloc. At the Shenzhen summit last week with the authoritarian Xi Jinping and the warmonger Vladimir Putin, Trump rejoiced that “we are making history.” The next day the US president upbraided Europe’s so-called Coalition of the Willing, including British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, for wasting billions of dollars defending Ukraine against his Kremlin “friend.”
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivens

item.title: UK Gen Z Workers Are Often Too Expensive to Hire
item.description: Apparently, you can tell who’s likeliest to spend a lifetime on welfare payments from the age of four or five. That’s one of the more arresting elements in a new UK review aimed at getting young adults into work, something the country has struggled to do for years.
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: Anthropic Billionaires Are Creating a New Type of AI Groupthink Hazard
item.description: When Dario Amodei rang the Nasdaq bell last week, marking a stock-market debut that proved just how tightly America’s economy is bound to its artificial intelligence pioneers, he was surrounded by his fellow Anthropic PBC founders and executives.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson

item.title: Advances in Animal Tracking Could Make Peace Between Man and Nature
item.description: Julia Roberts, Meryl Streep and George Clooney are currently on a long fishing trip in the Weddell Sea off the coast of Antarctica, diving for fish, krill and squid.
item.dc:creator: Lara Williams

item.title: Market Selloff: Just Be Thankful It’s a Short Week
item.description: No single factor caused the epic selloff, but pressure is now on the Fed.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Nvidia, S&P 500 Face Risks From US China AI Chip Curbs
item.description: Can the US crush China’s artificial-intelligence dreams without hurting itself? This is the question politicians in Washington must ask themselves. The blow to China is severe. The US has closed a long-standing loophole that allowed Chinese AI labs remote access to advanced American chips sold overseas. item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.title: AI Is Sucking Turbines From Other Industries
item.description: What connects a $3.7 billion writedown at SoftBank; the second-biggest takeover in General Electric’s history; the revival of a 250-year-old British industrial company; delays to container ships and a promised supersonic airliner; construction problems at power stations on two continents; and soaring natural gas pipeline costs?The answer is the artificial intelligence boom — and its insatiable hunger for energy.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: Japan’s Quantum Dawn Is Here. Now Comes the Hard Part
item.description: It wasn’t immediately clear whether I was stepping into the past or the future when I got a peek at a computer that took up an entire room. But, as in quantum mechanics, it felt as if two possibilities could exist at once.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Thorbecke

item.title: COP31: Climate Summit Fails When It Can’t Even Say ‘Fossil Fuels’
item.description: The 31st United Nations climate conference was expected to be a fairly dull affair, focusing on “implementation.” Instead, it will be one for the history books as a dramatic final showdown failed to result in an agreement for only the second time since climate COPs began in 1995.
item.dc:creator: Lara Williams

item.title: Newsom’s AI Populism Is a Bid to Stay Relevant
item.description: Now that the midterm elections are over, attention among those who just can’t get enough of politics has inevitably shifted to the 2028 presidential race. Who’s running? Who’s not running? These questions will be answered in the coming weeks and months.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: Rubio 2028 Rumors: Can He Restore the Republican Party?
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is suddenly everywhere, all at once. At the president’s side for his meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Briefing reporters on cyber glitches that have, in theory, nothing to do with his day job as secretary of state. All over the headlines as a new round of polls shows more Republicans want him to succeed President Donald Trump than want Vice President JD Vance or other Republicans to do so.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Electric? Luxury? Driverless? Your Car’s Falling Apart Anyway
item.description: The entire auto industry may be in a funk, but at least gasoline prices are down.
item.dc:creator: Toby Harshaw
